facts.statement: The genus Herrerasaurus was first described by Osvaldo Reig in 1963.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Reig, 1963

facts.statement: The name Herrerasaurus means "Herrera's lizard" and honors the rancher who found the first specimen in 1958.
facts.quote: Its name means "Herrera's lizard", after the rancher who discovered the first specimen in 1958 in South America.

facts.statement: All known fossils of Herrerasaurus come from the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina, dating to the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic approximately 231.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: All known fossils of this carnivore have been discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation of Carnian age (late Triassic according to the ICS, dated to 231.4 million years ago) in northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus measured about 6 meters in length and weighed approximately 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Measuring 6 m long and weighing around 350 kg, this genus was one of the earliest dinosaurs from the fossil record.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus belongs to the family Herrerasauridae, which includes some of the earliest genera in the dinosaur evolutionary radiation.
facts.quote: It is a member of the Herrerasauridae, a family of similar genera that were among the earliest of the dinosaurian evolutionary radiation.

facts.statement: Osvaldo Reig named the dinosaur after Victorino Herrera, a goatherd who discovered fossils near San Juan, Argentina, in 1959.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus was named by paleontologist Osvaldo Reig after Victorino Herrera, an Andean goatherd who first noticed its fossils in outcrops near the city of San Juan, Argentina, in 1959.

facts.statement: Fernando Novas named the species Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis in 1986, but it is now considered a synonym of Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: Two other partial skeletons with skull material were named Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis by Fernando Novas in 1986, but this species, too, is now thought to be a synonym.

facts.statement: A nearly complete Herrerasaurus skull was discovered in 1988 by a team led by Paul Sereno.
facts.quote: A complete Herrerasaurus skull was found in 1988 by a team of paleontologists led by Paul Sereno.

facts.statement: There is a persistent scientific debate over whether Herrerasaurus is a primitive theropod or a basal saurischian, with different researchers supporting each view.
facts.quote: However, Sereno favored classifying Herrerasaurus (and the Herrerasauridae) as primitive theropods. These two classifications have become the most persistent, with Rauhut (2003) and Bittencourt and Kellner (2004) favoring the early theropod hypothesis, and Max Langer (2004), Langer and Benton (2006), and Randall Irmis and his coauthors (2007) favoring the basal saurischian hypothesis.

facts.statement: If Herrerasaurus is a theropod, it suggests that theropods, sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians diverged before the middle Carnian and independently evolved features like advanced ankle joints.
facts.quote: If Herrerasaurus were indeed a theropod, it would indicate that theropods, sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians diverged even earlier than herrerasaurids, before the middle Carnian, and that "all three lineages independently evolved several dinosaurian features, such as a more advanced ankle joint or an open acetabulum".

facts.statement: Ichnological records of large three-toed footprints from the early Carnian Los Rastros Formation support the hypothesis that Herrerasaurus was a theropod.
facts.quote: This view is further supported by ichnological records showing large tridactyl (three-toed) footprints that can be attributed only to a theropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: Adult Herrerasaurus reached a total length of up to 6 meters, a skull length of 56 centimeters, and a weight of 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Adults had skulls up to 56 cm long and were up to 6 m in total length and 350 kg in weight.

facts.statement: Smaller specimens of Herrerasaurus measured approximately 4.5 meters in length and weighed about 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: Smaller specimens were about 4.5 m long and weighed about 200 kg.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was a fully bipedal carnivore with strong hind limbs and long feet that suggest it was a swift runner.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus was fully bipedal. It had strong hind limbs with short thighs and rather long feet, indicating that it was likely a swift runner.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a tail stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections that served to balance the body and aid in speed.
facts.quote: The tail, partially stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections, balanced the body and was also an adaptation for speed.

facts.statement: The first two fingers and the thumb of Herrerasaurus ended in curved, sharp claws used for grasping prey.
facts.quote: The first two fingers and the thumb ended in curved, sharp claws for grasping prey.

facts.statement: The fourth and fifth digits of the hand were small stubs without claws.
facts.quote: The fourth and fifth digits were small stubs without claws.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus possessed a long, narrow skull that lacked the specializations of later dinosaurs and resembled the skulls of primitive archosaurs like Euparkeria.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus had a long, narrow skull that lacked nearly all the specializations that characterized later dinosaurs, and more closely resembled those of more primitive archosaurs such as Euparkeria.

facts.statement: The skull of Herrerasaurus contained five pairs of fenestrae, two of which were for the eyes and nostrils.
facts.quote: It had five pairs of fenestrae (skull openings) in its skull, two pairs of which were for the eyes and nostrils.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had large serrated teeth for eating flesh and a slender, flexible neck.
facts.quote: The jaws were equipped with large serrated teeth for biting and eating flesh, and the neck was slender and flexible.

facts.statement: According to Novas (1993), Herrerasaurus is distinguished by features including a premaxilla-maxilla fenestra, a ridge on the jugal bone, a deeply incised supratemporal fossa, a trough-shaped ventral margin on the pterygoid process, enlarged hands that are 60% the size of the humerus plus radius, and a right angle formed by the posterior border of the ilial peduncle and the dorsal border of the ischium shaft.
facts.quote: According to Novas (1993), Herrerasaurus can be distinguished based on the following features: the presence of a premaxilla-maxilla fenestra, and the dorsal part of laterotemporal fenestra is less than a third as wide as the ventral part; the presence of a ridge on the lateral surface of the jugal bone, and a deeply incised supratemporal fossa that extends across the medial postorbital process; the subquadrate ventral squamosal process has a lateral depression, and the quadratojugal bone overlaps the posterodorsal quadrate face; the pterygoid process of the quadrate has an inturned, trough-shaped ventral margin, and the presence of a slender ribbed posterodorsal dentary process; the surangular bone has a forked anterior process for articulation with the posterodorsal dentary process; the humerus' internal tuberosity is proximally projected and separated from the humeral head by a deep groove (also present in coelophysoids); possesses enlarged hands, which are 60% of the size of the humerus+radius, and the humeral entepicondyle is ridge-like with anterior and posterior depressions; and the posterior border of the ilial peduncle forms a right angle with the dorsal border of the shaft on the ischium.

facts.statement: According to Sereno (1993), Herrerasaurus is distinguished by features unknown in other herrerasaurids, such as a circular pit on the humeral ectepicondyle, a saddle-shaped ulnar condyle, and a broad subnarial process of the premaxilla.
facts.quote: According to Sereno (1993), Herrerasaurus can be distinguished based on the following features, all of which are unknown in other herrerasaurids: a circular pit is present on the humeral ectepicondyle, a feature also present in Saturnalia; a saddle-shaped ulnar condyle of the humerus, and the articular surface for the ulnare on the ulna is convex; the articular surface of the ulnare is smaller than that of the ulna, a feature unknown in Staurikosaurus and Sanjuansaurus; the centrale is placed distal to the radiale; a broad subnarial process of the premaxilla, and a broad supratemporal depression (noted by Sereno and Novas, 1993); the basal tuber and the occipital condyle are subequal in width (noted by Sereno and Novas, 1993).

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus displays traits found in different groups of dinosaurs and non-dinosaurian archosaurs, sharing most dinosaur characteristics but differing in hip and leg bone shapes.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus displays traits that are found in different groups of dinosaurs, and several traits found in non-dinosaurian archosaurs. Although it shares most of the characteristics of dinosaurs, there are a few differences, particularly in the shape of its hip and leg bones.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a pelvis like saurischian dinosaurs, but its bony acetabulum was only partially open.
facts.quote: Its pelvis is like that of saurischian dinosaurs, but it has a bony acetabulum (where the femur meets the pelvis) that was only partially open.

facts.statement: The ilium of Herrerasaurus was supported by only two sacrals, which is a basal trait.
facts.quote: The ilium, the main hip bone, is supported by only two sacrals, a basal trait.

facts.statement: The pubis of Herrerasaurus pointed backwards, a derived trait seen in dromaeosaurids and birds.
facts.quote: However, the pubis points backwards, a derived trait as seen in dromaeosaurids and birds.

facts.statement: The end of the pubis in Herrerasaurus had a booted shape like avetheropods, and its vertebral centra had an hourglass shape found in Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Additionally, the end of the pubis has a booted shape, like those in avetheropods; and the vertebral centra have an hourglass shape as found in Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was originally classified within Carnosauria, a group that included animals similar to Megalosaurus and Antrodemus.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus was originally considered to be a genus within Carnosauria, which then included forms similar to Megalosaurus and Antrodemus

facts.statement: In 1966, Romer classified Herrerasaurus as a prosauropod possibly belonging to the family Plateosauridae.
facts.quote: Romer (1966), simply noted that Herrerasaurus was a prosauropod possibly within Plateosauridae

facts.statement: In 1996, Novas supported a theropod classification for Herrerasaurus, placing it closer to Neotheropoda than to Eoraptor or Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: In 1996, Novas went further by supporting a theropod position for Herrerasaurus with a phylogenetic analysis, which placed it closer to Neotheropoda than Eoraptor or Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: In 2004, Langer found through phylogenetic analysis that Herrerasaurus was more likely a basal saurischian than a theropod or a non-dinosaurian.
facts.quote: Langer (2004) conducted a phylogenetic analysis, and found that it was much more likely that Herrerasaurus was a basal saurischian, than either a theropod or a non-dinosaurian

facts.statement: In 2011, Martinez and colleagues described Eodromaeus, a basal theropod found in the same geological formation as Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2011, Martinez et al. described Eodromaeus, a basal theropod from the same formation as Herrerasaurus

facts.statement: Potential members of the Herrerasauridae clade may include Chindesaurus from Arizona and possibly Caseosaurus from Texas, though their relationships are not fully understood.
facts.quote: Other members of the clade may include Chindesaurus from the Upper Petrified Forest (Chinle Formation) of Arizona, and possibly Caseosaurus from the Tecovas Formation of the Dockum Group in Texas

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was a carnivore that preyed on small and medium-sized plant eaters based on its teeth and size.
facts.quote: The teeth of Herrerasaurus indicate that it was a carnivore; its size indicates it would have preyed upon small and medium-sized plant eaters

facts.statement: Dental microwear patterns suggest Herrerasaurus may have swallowed small prey whole with minimal oral processing, similar to modern crocodylians.
facts.quote: The similarity of its dental microwear patterns to those of modern slender-snouted crocodylians and small-bodied broad-snouted crocodylians, however, indicates that Herrerasaurus may have mainly consumed small prey that could have been swallowed whole with very minimal or no oral processing

facts.statement: Coprolites found in the Ischigualasto Formation containing small bones but no plant fragments are assigned to Herrerasaurus, indicating it could digest bone.
facts.quote: Coprolites (fossilized dung) containing small bones but no trace of plant fragments, discovered in the Ischigualasto Formation, have been assigned to Herrerasaurus based on fossil abundance

facts.statement: A 2001 study examined 12 hand bones and 20 foot bones of Herrerasaurus and found no signs of stress fractures.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 12 hand bones and 20 foot bones referred to Herrerasaurus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found

facts.statement: A Herrerasaurus skull (PVSJ 407) bears bite pits on the skull and splenial, with surrounding tissue suggesting a short-lived non-lethal infection, likely from a fight with another Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: PVSJ 407, a Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, had a pit in a skull bone attributed by Paul Sereno and Novas to a bite. Two additional pits occurred on the splenial. The areas around these pits are swollen and porous, suggesting the wounds were afflicted by a short-lived non-lethal infection

facts.statement: In 1985, Charig noted that Herrerasaurus had uncertain classification due to similarities to both prosauropods and carnosaurians.
facts.quote: In 1985, Charig noted that Herrerasaurus was of uncertain classification, showing similarities to both "prosauropods" and "carnosaurians"

facts.statement: In 2010, Alcocer and Martinez described Sanjuansaurus, a new herrerasaurid distinguished from Herrerasaurus by multiple features.
facts.quote: In 2010, Alcocer and Martinez described a new taxon of herrerasaurid, Sanjuansaurus. It could be distinguished from Herrerasaurus based on multiple features

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PVL 2566 was found in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in San Juan, Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype of Herrerasaurus (PVL 2566) was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in San Juan, Argentina.

facts.statement: Victorino Herrera collected the holotype specimen in 1961.
facts.quote: It was collected in 1961 by Victorino Herrera

facts.statement: The sediments containing the holotype were deposited during the Carnian stage of the Triassic, approximately 231 to 229 million years ago.
facts.quote: sediments that were deposited in the Carnian stage of the Triassic period, approximately 231 to 229 million years ago

facts.statement: A.S. Romer discovered specimen MCZ 7063 in 1958, which was originally referred to Staurikosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1958, A.S. Romer discovered specimen MCZ 7063, originally referred to Staurikosaurus in Carnian sediments.

facts.statement: Scaglia collected specimen PVL 2558 in 1961 from Carnian beds of the Ischigualasto Formation.
facts.quote: In 1961, Scaglia collected Herrerasaurus specimen PVL 2558, in the Carnian beds of this formation.

facts.statement: Additional Herrerasaurus specimens were found in the Cancha de Bochas Member in 1990.
facts.quote: In 1990, the Cancha de Bochas Member produced more Herrerasaurus specimens, also from its Carnian beds.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus lived during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 231.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió en el Carniense, a principios del período Triásico superior, hace aproximadamente 231,4 millones de años

facts.statement: Remains of Herrerasaurus were found in the Valle de la Luna in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en el Valle de la Luna del noroeste de Argentina.

facts.statement: The type species Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis was described by Osvaldo Alfredo Reig in 1963.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, fue descrita por Osvaldo Alfredo Reig en 1963

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis is the only known species of the extinct genus Herrerasaurus, a saurischian dinosaur belonging to the family Herrerasauridae.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis (lat. "lagarto de Herrera de Ischigualasto") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Herrerasaurus de dinosaurio saurisquio herrerasáurido

facts.statement: Recent examinations of theropod evolution have classified Herrerasaurus as an early theropod or an early saurischian.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus fue clasificado como un terópodo temprano o un saurisquio temprano en por lo menos cinco exámenes recientes de la evolución de los terópodos

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus is one of the most primitive known dinosaurs, described as a lightly built bipedal carnivore with a long tail and relatively small head.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus es uno de los dinosaurios más primitivos de los que se tengan registros, era un carnívoro bípedo ligeramente construido con una cola larga y una cabeza relativamente pequeña.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus had a femur length of about 50 centimeters, a total length between 3 and 6 meters, a hip height of 1.1 meters, and a weight between 210 and 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Presenta un tamaño medio, con el fémur de unos 50 centímetros de longitud, y un largo total de entre 3 y 6 metros, y una altura a las caderas de 1,1 metros, llegando a pesar entre 210 a 350 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The largest specimen was initially considered a separate genus, Frenguellisaurus, with a skull measuring about 56 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El mayor espécimen en un principio fue considerado un género separado, Frenguellisaurus, cuyo cráneo medía unos 56 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The neck of Herrerasaurus shows no signs of elongation and is described as quite short and strong.
facts.quote: El cuello del Herrerasaurus no muestra signos de elongación. Es bastante corto y fuerte.

facts.statement: The sacral bone is considered primitive because it is composed of only three vertebrae.
facts.quote: El hueso sacro es primitivo por las pocas vértebras que lo integran, solo tres.

facts.statement: The ilium, the main bone of the pelvis, is supported by only two sacral vertebrae, a basal trait.
facts.quote: El ilion, el hueso principal de la cadera, está soportado por solo dos vértebras sacras, un rasgo basal.

facts.statement: The pubis points backward, a derived trait seen in dromaeosaurids and birds.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el pubis apunta hacia atrás, un rasgo derivado como se ve en los dromeosáuridos y las aves.

facts.statement: The pubis ends in a boot-like shape similar to avetheropods, and the vertebral centrum has an hourglass shape similar to that found in Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Además, el final del pubis tiene una forma de bota, como las de los aveterópodos y el centro vertebral tiene una forma de reloj de arena como el que se encuentra en el Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Vegetation included ferns (Cladophlebis), horsetails, and giant conifers (Protojuniperoxylon).
facts.quote: Vegetation consisted of ferns (Cladophlebis), horsetails, and giant conifers (Protojuniperoxylon).

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus lived in Late Triassic South American jungles alongside early dinosaurs like Sanjuansaurus and Eoraptor, as well as rhynchosaurs, cynodonts, dicynodonts, pseudosuchians, proterochampsids, and temnospondyls.
facts.quote: It lived in the jungles of Late Triassic South America alongside other early dinosaurs, such as Sanjuansaurus, Eoraptor, Panphagia, and Chromogisaurus, as well as rhynchosaurs (Scaphonyx), cynodonts (e.g., Exaeretodon, Ecteninion and Chiniquodon), dicynodonts (Ischigualastia), pseudosuchians (e.g., Saurosuchus, Sillosuchus and Aetosauroides), proterochampsids (e.g., Proterochampsa) and temnospondyls (Pelorocephalus).

facts.statement: Historically, hypotheses debated whether Herrerasaurus was a basal theropod, a basal sauropodomorph, a basal saurischian, or even a non-dinosaur.
facts.quote: Esto conllevó la emisión de diversas hipótesis taxonómicas encuadrándolos como un terópodo basal, un sauropodomorfo basal, un saurisquio basal, o inclusive un no dinosaurio.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Herrerasaurus is Reig, 1963.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Reig, 1963

facts.statement: The species authority for Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis is Reig, 1963.
facts.quote: species_authority: Reig, 1963

facts.statement: Synonyms for Herrerasaurus include Ischisaurus cattoi and Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis.
facts.quote: synonyms: Ischisaurus cattoi Reig, 1963 Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis Novas, 1986

facts.statement: Adult Herrerasaurus reached lengths of up to 6 meters and weighed up to 350 kilograms.
facts.quote: Los adultos tenían cráneos de hasta 56 centímetros de largo y tenían hasta 6 metros de longitud total y 350 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: The skull was narrow and long, lacking most specializations found in later dinosaurs and resembling earlier archosaurs like Euparkeria.
facts.quote: El cráneo es estrecho y largo y carecía de casi todas las especializaciones que caracterizaron a los dinosaurios posteriores, no tan diferente al de los arcosaurios anteriores como Euparkeria.

facts.statement: A flexible joint between the dentary and postdentary bones allowed the lower jaw to slide forward and backward, creating a crushing bite.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus poseía una articulación flexible entre los huesos dentarios y postdentarios, esto permitió que el animal resbalara su quijada inferior hacia adelante y hacia atrás y dar una mordedura de compresión.

facts.statement: The jaws were equipped with large serrated teeth for biting and eating meat, and the neck was thin and flexible.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas fueron equipadas de los dientes serrados grandes para morder y comer carne, y el cuello era delgado y flexible.

facts.statement: Based on its dental arrangement, researchers infer that the front teeth were used for catching and killing prey.
facts.quote: A raíz de estos caracteres se puede inferir que la acción de atrapar y matar a la presa era trabajo de los dientes anteriores.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was completely bipedal.
facts.quote: Herrerasaurus era completamente bípedo.

facts.statement: It had strong hind limbs with short thighs and fairly long feet, indicating it was likely a fast runner.
facts.quote: Tenía miembros posteriores fuertes con muslos cortos y pies bastante largos, lo que indica que probablemente era un corredor veloz.

facts.statement: The foot had five toes, but only the three central digits (II, III, and IV) supported weight.
facts.quote: El pie tenía cinco dedos, pero solo los tres medios, los dígitos II, III y IV, soportaban peso.

facts.statement: The first two toes and the thumb ended in curved, sharp claws for grabbing prey.
facts.quote: Los primeros dos dedos y el pulgar terminaron en garras curvas y afiladas para agarrar la presa.

facts.statement: The tail, partially stiffened by overlapping vertebral projections, balanced the body and was an adaptation for speed.
facts.quote: La cola, parcialmente rígida por las proyecciones vertebrales superpuestas, equilibró el cuerpo y también fue una adaptación para la velocidad.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Herrerasaurus were less than half the length of its hind limbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores de Herrerasaurus tenían menos de la mitad de la longitud de sus extremidades traseras.

facts.statement: It possessed three elongated fingers, the third being the longest with strong claws that closed over the palm to grasp prey, while fingers IV and V were very small and clawless.
facts.quote: Esta poseía tres dedos alargados, el tercero es el más largo con fuertes garras que se cerraban sobre la palma permitiéndole tomar a sus presas, los dedos IV y V son muy pequeños y sin garras.

facts.statement: A fenestra between the premaxilla and maxilla is present, and the dorsal part of the laterotemporal fenestra is less than one-third the width of the ventral part.
facts.quote: La presencia de una fenestra entre el premaxilar y el maxilar, y la parte dorsal de la fenestra laterotemporal es menos de un tercio del ancho de la parte ventral de la misma.

facts.statement: It possessed elongated hands, which are equivalent in size to 60% of the humerus and radius, and the entepicondyle of the humerus has a crest shape with anterior and posterior depressions.
facts.quote: Posee manos alargadas, las cuales tienen un tamaño equivalente al 60% del húmero y el radio, y el entepocóndilo del húmero tiene forma de cresta con depresiones anteriores y posteriores.

facts.statement: A circular incision is present on the ectepicondyle of the humerus, a trait also found in Saturnalia.
facts.quote: Una incisión circular presente en el ectepicóndilo del húmero, un rasgo también presente en Saturnalia

facts.statement: The central bone is situated distally relative to the radial bone.
facts.quote: El central se sitúa distalmente con respecto al radial.

facts.statement: A wide subnarial process on the premaxilla and a wide supratemporal depression are noted by Sereno and Novas (1993).
facts.quote: Un amplio proceso subnarial en el premaxilar, y una ancha depresión supratemporal, señalado por Sereno y Novas, 1993.

facts.statement: Eoraptor from the same Ischigualasto Formation in Argentina where Herrerasaurus was found may be included in the same clade.
facts.quote: Otros miembros del clado pueden incluir a Eoraptor de la misma Formación Ischigualasto de Argentina en que se halló a Herrerasaurus

facts.statement: Gregory Paul (1988) suggested Staurikosaurus pricei was incorrectly identified as a juvenile Herrerasaurus, but this was refuted when young Herrerasaurus pelvic bones were found to lack resemblance to Staurikosaurus pelvis.
facts.quote: Gregory Paul en 1988 sugirió que se había señalado incorrectamente que Staurikosaurus pricei era un juvenil de Herrerasaurus. Esta afirmación fue refutada cuando los huesos pélvicos de un ejemplar joven de Herrerasaurus fueron descubiertos, que al ser examinados no revelaron ningún parecido particular a los de la pelvis de Staurikosaurus.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus was a carnivore that hunted small to medium-sized animals based on its teeth and size.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Herrerasaurus indican que eran carnívoros, su tamaño indica que habrían cazado pequeños y medianos animales.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus may have preyed on other dinosaurs, including the herbivore Pisanosaurus.
facts.quote: Se pudieron haber alimentado de otros dinosaurios, tales como el herbívoro Pisanosaurus.

facts.statement: Because dinosaurs were rare during its time, Herrerasaurus likely included abundant rhynchosaurs and herbivorous synapsids in its diet.
facts.quote: ya que Herrerasaurus vivió durante una era cuando otros dinosaurios eran infrecuentes, habría incluido entre sus presas los más abundantes rincosáuridos y sinápsidos herbívoros.

facts.statement: Fossilized coprolites attributed to Herrerasaurus contain small bones but no plant fragments, indicating it could digest bones.
facts.quote: Se han descubierto coprolitos, estiércol fosilizado, que contienen pequeños huesos pero ningún rastro de fragmentos de plantas en la formación de Ischigualasto, asignándose a Herrerasaurus de acuerdo con su abundancia fósil.

facts.statement: Comparisons of scleral rings suggest Herrerasaurus may have been catemeral, active throughout the day in short intervals.
facts.quote: Las comparaciones entre los anillos esclerales de Herrerasaurus y las aves y reptiles modernos sugieren que puede haber sido catemeral, activo durante todo el día a intervalos cortos.

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus lived about 230 million years ago, during a time when dinosaurs were small and insignificant compared to other reptiles.
facts.quote: vivió cerca de hace 230 millones de años, una época en que los dinosaurios eran pequeños e insignificantes.

facts.statement: At the time in Ischigualasto, dinosaurs made up only 6% of the total fossils found.
facts.quote: Para ese momento, en Ischigualasto los dinosaurios constituían solo el 6% del total de los fósiles.

facts.statement: The genus Herrerasaurus was named by Reig in 1963.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Herrerasaurus (genus), Reig 1963

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus belongs to the family Herrerasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Herrerasauridae

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Herrerasaurus lived during the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: A specimen of Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis (PVSJ 407) had a cranial bone incision attributed to a bite by Paul Sereno and Fernando Novas.
facts.quote: PVSJ 407, un ejemplar de Herrerasaurus ischigualastensis, tenía una incisión en un hueso craneal atribuida por Paul Sereno y Fernando Novas a una mordida.

facts.statement: Two additional holes in the splenial bone showed swelling and porosity, suggesting a short-duration non-lethal infection.
facts.quote: Dos agujeros más aparecen en el esplenial. Las áreas alrededor de los agujeros están hinchadas y son porosas, lo que sugiere que las heridas sufrieron una infección no letal de corta duración.

facts.statement: Based on the size and angle of the wounds, it is probable they were inflicted during a fight with another Herrerasaurus.
facts.quote: Tomando en cuenta el tamaño y el ángulo de las heridas, es probable que fueran infligidas durante una lucha con otro Herrerasaurus.
